angularDiameterSource: Computed: the volume-equivalent radius of Che et al. 2011's polar and equatorial radii at the Hipparcos distance; the paper fits the radii, not a single diameter.
distanceSource: Inverse of the Hipparcos new-reduction parallax 41.13 ± 0.35 mas (van Leeuwen 2007) via SIMBAD
radiusSource: Radius: the volume-equivalent sphere of the polar radius 3.22^{+0.05}_{-0.04} and equatorial radius 4.21^{+0.07}_{-0.06} solar radii of Che et al. 2011 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.0740), Table 4, modified von Zeipel model (beta free); the scene draws the flattening. presentationUp: the measured rotation pole is up.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 12901 ± 500 K, the surface-mean value <T> of McAlister et al. 2005 (ApJ 628, 439; https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0501261), Table 5.
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the model mass 4.15 ± 0.06 solar masses of Che et al. 2011 (ApJ 732, 68; https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.0740), Table 4, and the volume-equivalent radius, log10(GM/R^2) in cgs

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray; the photosphere of a giant star is not a solid surface and its limb is not sharp.
